content: Chondrolecitin is a protein in humans encoded by the CHODL gene. In mice, the corresponding protein is encoded by the Chodl gene. Chondrolecitin is classified as a type I membrane protein. It contains a carbohydrate recognition domain in its extracellular region, which is characteristic of C-type lectins. In other proteins, this domain is known to play a role in the endocytosis of glycoproteins and sugar-bearing exogenous pathogens. Chondrolecitin has been observed to localize to the perinuclear region of cells. The precise function of chondrolecitin remains unclear. However, it has been identified as a marker of fast motor neurons in mice and is implicated in the development and growth of motor neurons in zebrafish (Danio rerio). Additionally, in humans, chondrolecitin has been shown to localize specifically to motor neurons within the spinal cord. Chondrolecitin undergoes alternative splicing in the spinal cord of mouse models of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), a neuromuscular disease that primarily affects lower motor neurons. In a zebrafish model of SMA, increased levels of chondrolecitin have been associated with significant improvements in motor neuron defects related to the disease.
